english.title: Behave / hold self out as person to whom a section 333 general prohibition does not apply
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[behaved]_
(B)_[held yourself out]_

in a manner which indicated or which was reasonably likely to be understood as indicating that you were a person to whom the general prohibition in section 19 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 did not apply in relation to a particular related activity, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACTIVITY..), as a result of Part XX of that Act when you were not such a person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 333(1)(b) and (3) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) In proceedings for an offence under section 333 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 it is a defence for the accused to show that he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the committing the offence.
(ii) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the Authority or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
